title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
keyIdea: Put everything in a hash set. Only start counting from numbers whose num − 1 is missing (run starts), then walk up with st.count(curr + 1). Each number is visited by exactly one run, so it's O(n).

approaches.name: Brute force with linear search
approaches.idea: From every number, look for x + 1, x + 2, … with a linear scan.
approaches.why: Up to n starts × up to n steps × O(n) search each.

approaches.name: Hash set, count only from run starts
approaches.idea: st = set(nums). For each num with num − 1 not in st, count up while curr + 1 is in st; track the longest.
approaches.why: Each number is counted inside exactly one run; set lookups are O(1) on average.

quiz.q: Why only start when num − 1 is missing?
options: Otherwise runs would be re-counted from the middle, making it O(n²)

quiz.q: Why loop over the set instead of nums?
options: Duplicates are removed, so a start isn't processed twice
